symptom: An import or export mapping element `Assoc/Entity` whose association did not connect the entity above it to its own entity passed `check` and `exec` and was written; `mx check` then reported CE0295 "Association '...' is not allowed". Neither-end, parent-only and element-only associations were all rejected; the matching pair, and an end that is a generalization of the parent, the element's entity or both, built clean.
file: mdl/executor/validate_mapping_associations.go ValidateMappingAssociations (MDL100), called from validate_program.go with the lazy project opener. Tests: validate_mapping_associations_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-association-not-allowed(.fail).mdl
cause: The export and import mapping builders resolve nothing about an element's association beyond qualifying its name; the message-definition path already refuses an association that connects neither direction (resolveAssociationCardinality), but the mapping builders never got that check. The four existing CE0295 findings were all the same mxcli-written array-container bug, so the rule for hand-written mappings was never recorded.
insight: **When the field-hit ranking shows a code only in findings about mxcli's own writer, the user-script form of the same error is probably unrefused: measure the hand-written shapes before assuming the writer fix covered it.** Measured on MxBuild 11.16.1 in separate project copies (export and import, one defect per copy plus a control): neither end, parent-only and element-only are CE0295; the plain pair is clean; specialization of the parent, the element or both is clean. My first control was wrong - an object element over a plain many-to-one Reference is also CE0295 (the association must reach at most one object; the repo's own example uses owner both) - which is a separate cardinality rule left uncovered, and the reason to run a control before trusting it. The resolver reuses associationCatalogFor and findEntityByQN, keeps the spelling the names were written in for project lookups (lower-casing them made the chain read as unreadable and the rule silent), and refuses only when both generalization chains were read to their roots. Sweep: 1,314 repo .mdl files, 0 MDL100 hits (weak without a project; the measurement is the evidence). Control: stubbing the function fails the script, group, project and parent-specialization tests.
